links.outcome: High-risk patients receiving remote monitoring equipment, model-based selection versus random allocation in simulated weekly distribution
links.effect: Model-based selection led to more high-risk patients receiving remote monitoring equipment than random allocation (no numbers given in the abstract).
links.quote: Compared to the random resource allocation, the selection of patients with respect to the outputs of the proposed model was proven beneficial, as it led to a higher number of high-risk patients receiving remote monitoring equipment.

links.outcome: AUROC on patient-grouped random split versus temporally later (last year) test set
links.effect: AUROC was 69.5% on the patient-grouped 70/30 split and 65.3% on the last-year test set, a lower value on the later data.
links.quote: The achieved Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve on these test sets was 69.5% and 65.3%, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Involving clinicians in data preparation and pipeline optimization for a predictive model

screen.reason: The study develops a predictive risk model and simulates a real-world resource allocation policy (decision support for remote patient monitoring distribution) comparing model-guided selection against random allocation.

primary.practice: AI-guided resource allocation vs random allocation
